claims.statement: EU electricity-market rules define independent aggregation and require Member States to allow demand response through aggregation and non-discriminatory participation in electricity markets.

Poland operates a balancing-market segment administered by PSE to cover balance-adjusting actions and settlements, but technical qualification and balance responsibility remain material entry constraints.

Hypothesis: fragmented SME loads can produce attractive net revenue after partner, telemetry, and customer shares once a portfolio reaches meaningful controllable capacity; a live shadow-dispatch pilot is essential before claiming economics.

contrary_evidence: The same EU rules make aggregators financially responsible for imbalances or require them to delegate that responsibility, which can absorb margin.
A small flexible asset may not justify integration, metering, qualification, and support costs.

economics.acquisition_route: Family installer and commercial-energy partners identify eligible sites; savings simulations and shadow-dispatch reports convert owners
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: control of 20-40 MW across several hundred sites, with recurring monitoring and a defensible share of flexibility value, could yield several million PLN of annual gross profit and over 5m PLN founder equity in five to nine years
economics.founder_time: Up to 20 hours weekly during a narrow shadow pilot; live operations require partner SLAs and hired monitoring before scale
economics.gross_margin_basis: Software gross margin can be high, but partner fees, telemetry hardware, support, and imbalance exposure could reduce blended contribution to 35-65%
economics.payback: No-upfront revenue share should give customers immediate payback; platform hardware and CAC should recover within 12-18 months only after shadow-pilot proof
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: retain 15-25% of net flexibility revenue plus 200-600 PLN monthly for monitoring or bill optimisation where independently valuable
economics.retention_or_repeat: Two-to-five-year dispatch-right contracts can retain capacity, while response history improves renewal and cross-selling

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Exclusive controllable-capacity contracts plus asset-level response, availability, and settlement history
fingerprint.customer: Polish SMEs with controllable batteries, EV chargers, HVAC, refrigeration, flexible process loads, or rooftop generation
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Renewable installers, energy auditors, equipment distributors, and ESCOs embed enrolment at installation or retrofit
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Portfolio monitoring, dispatch-right contracts, optimisation, and revenue sharing through a licensed route to market
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Market-access partner or energy buyer pays for delivered flexibility; customer and platform split verified revenue, with optional monitoring subscription
fingerprint.problem_trigger: An owner has underused flexible equipment or faces volatile energy costs and is offered a no-upfront revenue-share programme

founder_fit: High analytical and renewable-channel fit with asymmetric upside from contracted capacity rather than capital-intensive ownership. The founder can start with forecasting and shadow dispatch beside a full-time job, while licensed market access, controls engineering, and 24/7 operations stay with partners.
risks: Dispatch error could damage customer operations or equipment.
Market-rule, price, or partner changes could eliminate expected revenue.
Cybersecurity and remote-control obligations may exceed a part-time founder's safe operating capacity until a specialist team is hired.

structure.commercial_archetype: Asset-light flexibility aggregator and revenue-share network
structure.control_point: Contractual dispatch rights over a pooled portfolio and the proof of delivered response
structure.critical_dependency: A licensed route-to-market partner and unit economics that survive telemetry, settlement, and imbalance costs

thesis: Aggregate the contractual right and telemetry needed to shift small commercial batteries, EV charging, heat pumps, refrigeration, and rooftop generation, then monetise the pooled flexibility through a licensed balancing or energy-market partner. Begin as monitoring and optimisation software; build defensibility through exclusive, time-bounded dispatch rights and verified response history rather than owning energy assets.
title: SME Flex Rights Pool
uncertainties: The current Polish route, minimum bid sizes, and partner terms for each asset class.
How much reliable flexibility target SMEs can provide without disrupting operations.
Customer willingness to grant dispatch rights and accept cyber-connected controls.
